questions.history: Reduce the six-digit TIME cast and the analogous TIMESTAMP(6) cast for 2020-01-01 12:34:56.123456.
questions.prediction: The PR reports loss of digits past milliseconds on the parent. On the merge the returned time and timestamp strings should each end in .123456 with their whole-second and date components preserved.
questions.basis: All six digits fit the declared precision exactly. The pinned reducer tests exercise precisions 1 through 9.
questions.refutation: A nonliteral result for the fixture, a .123000 suffix, a changed date, or any other loss of representable digits.

questions.history: Reduce TIME(3) and TIMESTAMP(3) casts of the same whole-second values with exactly .123 in the inputs.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should return .123 when read as TimeString or TimestampString at precision three.
questions.basis: These values are exactly representable at millisecond precision.
questions.refutation: Either reduced literal loses or changes one of the three significant digits.

questions.history: Reduce a pair of timestamps differing only in the sixth fractional digit, .123456 and .123457. Cast each to VARCHAR(30), then reduce and read the result strings.
questions.prediction: On the merge the strings should respectively end .123456 and .123457. They must remain distinguishable after the temporal-to-character conversion.
questions.basis: The inputs differ by one representable microsecond. String readback tests the next consumer rather than only a temporal type's declared precision.
questions.refutation: Equal strings, a wrong last digit or a changed date on either path.
